entry.title: Towards New Self-Custody Best Practices
entry.summary:
Managing financial assets effectively involves tailoring security measures to the scale of the funds involved. For everyday balances, personal savings, and life savings, distinct levels of security complexity are justified. More substantial investments, such as life savings, may necessitate enhanced security protocols, including multi-vendor setups like a 2-of-2 configuration. This approach indeed mitigates certain risks by requiring multiple keys for access. However, it also complicates the backup process and increases the potential for user error during recovery operations.
Given these complexities, there is a compelling argument for establishing defined security guidelines tailored to the amount of funds being protected. Such guidelines should not only specify security measures but also mandate practical rehearsal of recovery procedures before any significant amounts of money are deposited. This practice would ensure that users are not only prepared to implement their backups but are also fully aware of all necessary details to facilitate a smooth recovery. Currently, a common oversight among users involves creating backups without verifying their ability to restore from them or confirming possession of all essential information needed for the process. This gap in security practices can lead to critical failures in accessing one's funds when needed most.
